plain.li: [for,subject] Someone should make sure {SUBJECT} stays in bed this time.
[for,subject] I looked in on {SUBJECT}, and they're in no state to work.
[for] The sick should be in bed, not dragging themselves round the fields.
[for] A day in bed now saves a week of it later.
[for,serious] This one can kill, and we're treating it like a cold.
[for,subjectserious] {SUBJECT} could die of this if we're careless.
[for,ill] I should be in bed, and I know it.
[for,wounded] This hurt won't heal if I keep pulling at it.
[for,doctor] My patients keep getting up the moment I turn my back.
[for,lowtech] Rest and broth by the fire, that's what the sick need.
[for,!lowtech] Rest, fluids and the medicine shelf, that's what the sick need.
[against] Lie down for every sniffle and nothing would ever get done.
[against,subject] {SUBJECT} is well enough to grumble, so they're well enough to work.
[against] The beds are for the badly hurt, not for anyone with a cough.
[against,ill] I'm not lying down for this, there's too much to do.
[against,wounded] It's a scratch, I've had worse and kept working.
[against] I worked through worse than this when I was young.
[against,lowtech] Our herbs are too few to waste on every cough.
[against,!lowtech] We can't spend the good medicine on every cough.
[mixed,subject] How is {SUBJECT} doing, have you heard?
[mixed] There's always someone ill in this place, have you noticed?
[mixed,serious] I don't like how this sickness is spreading.
[mixed] I can never tell who's really ill and who's just tired.

warm.li: [for,subject] I took {SUBJECT} some water and sat with them a while.
[for] Nobody should be sick and alone in this place.
[against] I worry about them, but the work has to go on somehow.
[mixed,subject] I hope {SUBJECT} is up and about again soon.

blunt.li: [for] Sick people in bed, it's simple.

cheerful.li: [for,ill] I'm going to enjoy every minute of being looked after.
[for] A warm bed and a bowl of soup cures most things, I say.
[against,wounded] Look at this, I'll have a scar to brag about.
[mixed] At least nobody's sick of my cooking yet.

gloomy.li: [for,serious] It'll be one of us next, mark me.
[against] Lie down out here and you might not get up again.
[mixed,ill] I feel like something the dog left.
[mixed] Someone's always ill, and someday it'll be the bad kind.

cold.li: [for] A sick worker who rests is back sooner, that's arithmetic.
[against] Every one of them in bed is a pair of hands we don't have.
[against,subject] {SUBJECT} has been in bed longer than the wound needs.
[mixed,doctor] I've counted the medicine, and we'll manage, barely.

plain.li: [agree,for] Bed and rest, and the work can wait.
[agree,for,subject] I'll make sure {SUBJECT} stays put.
[agree,for,otherill] Then go and lie down, and I'll cover your work.
[agree,against] Most of it you just work through, I've always said so.
[agree,against,otherwounded] You've had worse, I've seen it.
[agree,mixed] It's hard to know, I'll grant you.
[agree,serious] We should keep the sick apart from the rest, then.
[debate,for] Rest, yes, but not for a week over a cough.
[debate,against] Work, maybe, but not with a fever.
[debate,doctor] You'd let the healer decide, if you had any sense.
[debate] It depends on what they've got.
[argue,for] And who does their work, you?
[argue,against] Say that when it's you burning up in bed.
[argue,otherill] You're ill, and you're too stubborn to see it.
[argue] You'd have the sick dig their own graves, would you.

warm.li: [agree] I'll look in on them later.
[agree,otherill] Please lie down, for my sake.
[debate,against] I know you're worried about the work, but they come first.
[argue] I don't want to quarrel about sick people.

cheerful.li: [agree] I'll bring the soup, you bring the stories.
[agree,otherwounded] You'll heal faster if you stop showing it off.
[debate] Let's ask the patient, they'll want the bed.
[argue] Fine, the next time you sneeze, you're working.

gloomy.li: [agree,serious] We'll be lucky if it stops at one.
[debate] Bed or no bed, it does what it wants.
[agree] They looked bad, I'll say that.

cold.li: [debate] It's a question of how long they're down.
[argue,for] Sentiment won't bring the harvest in.
[argue,against] A dead worker does even less work.

plain.li: [agree] Let's hope they're up again soon.
[agree,for] I'll keep the work off them for a few days.
[agree,against] I'll get them back on light work tomorrow.
[agree,serious] Wash your hands, both of us.
[debate] We'll see how they are in the morning.
[debate,doctor] I'll look at them again tonight and decide.
[argue] Have it your way, then.
[argue,otherill] Lie down before you fall down.

warm.li: [debate] Let's both look in on them later.

cheerful.li: [argue] I'll save you a bed for when you catch it.

gloomy.li: [agree] Here's hoping it's not one of us next.

plain.li: [debate] I'll ask the healer what they think.
[debate,for] A day's rest never killed anyone.
[debate,against] A day's work never killed anyone either.
[argue] You'll want that bed yourself one day.
[argue,for] Wait till it's you, then tell me about working through it.
[argue,against] The fields don't care who's poorly.

warm.li: [debate] I just want them well, that's all.

cheerful.li: [debate] I'll bring them a game to keep them in bed.
[argue] I'm telling the healer you said that.

gloomy.li: [argue,serious] Don't say I didn't warn you.

plain.li: [otherill] You'll do anything to get out of the washing up, won't you, {OTHER}.
[otherwounded] Walked into a wall again, {OTHER}?
[otherfor] You'd put the whole colony to bed for a sneeze, {OTHER}.
[otheragainst] You'd work with one leg off and call it a sprain, {OTHER}.
[otherill] Your nose is the color of a ripe berry, {OTHER}.

cheerful.li: [otherwounded] I'll carve you a little medal for that hurt, {OTHER}.
[otherill] Shall I fluff your pillow for you, {OTHER}?
[otherfor] You'd tuck in the cattle if they coughed, {OTHER}.
